_meta.title: OMGPR test vectors (T016)
_meta.scope: Confirmed positive, negative, zero, scale, spaces, low-values, and error-field encode/decode vectors for a representative set of OMGPR fields, each citing its copybook definition from docs/mappings/omgpr-data-dictionary.csv (T003).
_meta.confidence_key: CONFIRMED = directly derived from the copybook PIC clause and a documented, standard COBOL encoding rule. INFERRED = a reasonable encoding choice where the standard rule has more than one documented convention. BLOCKED = cannot be determined without a live compile/runtime capture.
_meta.why_two_encoding_profiles: This codebase's programs carry pervasive 'MFMIGR' change-tags (e.g. A6X01.CBL, A6O012U.CBL: 'MODIFIED SET STATEMENT TO RETRIEVE CURRENT DATE IN ORDER TO WORK WITH ANSI COMPLIANT DBRM DATABASES') confirming a historical Micro Focus migration occurred. This is direct, in-source evidence -- not a hypothetical -- that the runtime character set and COMP binary byte order cannot be assumed to be traditional IBM mainframe EBCDIC/big-endian without a live capture. Every vector below is therefore encoded under BOTH a 'mainframe_ebcdic' profile (the traditional convention, and the one this project's byte-length arithmetic in T003/T004 already assumes for field SIZING) and a 'microfocus_ascii_native' profile (a documented alternate Micro Focus configuration). Field byte LENGTHS and OFFSETS are not in question (T003 already reconciled these against the 1,789-byte COMMAREA); only the byte CONTENT for a given logical value is profile-sensitive, and only for two of the four storage types used here.
standing_blockers: No live COBOL/CICS/DB2 execution environment exists to capture an authoritative COMMAREA byte dump -- every encoding below is derived from documented standard conventions, not observed runtime output (same standing blocker as every other document in this repository).

Which encoding profile this specific deployment actually uses is unresolved -- this is exactly the 'unknown encoding/byte order' T016's own acceptance criteria asks to be parameterized, not guessed. This is also Codex's G1 downstream blocker #2: 'Reconcile the OMGPR 1789-byte statement with an authoritative live compiler layout and COMMAREA capture before compatibility decoding begins.'

mainframe_ebcdic.description: Traditional IBM z/OS mainframe convention. Default/primary profile used for T003/T004's own byte-length arithmetic.
mainframe_ebcdic.charset: EBCDIC code page 037 (1 byte per DISPLAY character)
mainframe_ebcdic.comp3_convention: packed decimal: 2 BCD digits per byte except the final byte, which holds 1 digit plus a sign nibble (C=positive/signed, D=negative, F=unsigned)
mainframe_ebcdic.confidence: INFERRED (standard convention for the platform T003 already assumed for sizing; not independently confirmed for this specific deployment)

microfocus_ascii_native.description: Documented alternate Micro Focus COBOL configuration for open-systems (Windows/Unix) ports, consistent with this codebase's pervasive MFMIGR change-tags. Provided as the explicitly parameterized alternative, not asserted as more or less likely than mainframe_ebcdic.
microfocus_ascii_native.charset: ASCII / Windows-1252 (1 byte per DISPLAY character)
microfocus_ascii_native.comp_byte_order: little-endian two's-complement binary (Micro Focus 'native' binary format default on x86; can be configured for big-endian mainframe-compatible mode, which is a separate, third possibility this document does not attempt to enumerate)
microfocus_ascii_native.comp3_convention: packed decimal, same nibble/sign-byte layout as mainframe_ebcdic -- Micro Focus COBOL documents COMP-3 as packed-decimal-compatible with IBM mainframe by default, so this field TYPE is treated as low-ambiguity across both profiles, unlike DISPLAY charset and COMP byte order
microfocus_ascii_native.confidence: INFERRED (a documented possibility given the MFMIGR evidence; not confirmed as the actual configuration in use)

vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (standard EBCDIC cp037 / ASCII character mapping for digits and uppercase letters, mechanically applied)
CONFIRMED (space is the field's own declared VALUE clause default)

vectors.logical_value: LOW-VALUES (binary zeros, not a printable string)
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (LOW-VALUES is binary zero bytes, identical under any charset -- profile-independent by definition, included to demonstrate that low-values is NOT the same encoding question as spaces)

vectors.notes: Stored as text, not a COBOL date type. Layout inferred as MM/DD/YYYY by analogy to the substring-reassembly logic documented in docs/rules/date-selection.md's R-DATE-004 (positions 1-2=MM, 4-5=DD, 7-10=YYYY, with 1-character separators at positions 3 and 6) -- that layout is itself INFERRED, not confirmed by any copybook comment, and is repeated here rather than re-derived.
vectors.confidence: INFERRED (character encoding mechanism is CONFIRMED standard; the MM/DD/YYYY layout choice itself is INFERRED per date-selection.md)

vectors.notes: Represents a pricing date not yet supplied by the caller.
Flagged explicitly by Codex's G1 review as a field that must not be confused with the separate X(20) OMGPR-I-GRP-CNT-NBR field -- this is the pure-binary 4-byte contract number.
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (standard two's-complement binary encoding, mechanically computed; byte ORDER is the profile-sensitive axis, not the value)

vectors.notes: No source paragraph was found assigning a negative value to this specific field in this pass -- included to exercise the signed-COMP encoding rule itself (this field's PIC is S9(8), so a negative representation must be well-defined even if not observed in practice), not asserted as a value this field takes in production.
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (standard two's-complement encoding of the negative value, mechanically computed)

vectors.notes: Represents 'no contract selected' -- the field's own declared default.
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (zero is identical under either byte order)

vectors.notes: 13 total digits (5 integer + 8 decimal, V is an implied decimal point -- no byte is stored for it). Digit string '0012345678901' packs into 6 full-digit-pair bytes plus a final byte holding the 13th digit and the sign nibble.

encoded.mainframe_ebcdic: 00123456789 01C (shown with a space for readability; actual bytes: 00 12 34 56 78 90 1C)
encoded.microfocus_ascii_native: same as mainframe_ebcdic: 00 12 34 56 78 90 1C -- COMP-3 packing is treated as profile-independent (see encoding_profiles.microfocus_ascii_native.comp3_convention)

vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (standard packed-decimal encoding, mechanically computed from the digit string; sign nibble C = positive is the standard preferred-sign convention)

vectors.notes: Same digit packing as V-UNITCOST-01, sign nibble D instead of C.
The maximum value representable by this PIC clause -- all 13 digit positions at 9. Exercises the boundary the field's byte length was sized for.
Unsigned PIC (no S) -- sign nibble is F (the standard 'unsigned' sign value), never C or D. 5 total digits (1 integer + 4 decimal), digit string '01500'.

Maximum value representable. Cross-reference: docs/rules/sell-selection-rules.md's R-SELL-003 and docs/rules/fees-and-adjustments.md's R-DISTMKP-001 both document an explicit runtime clamp elsewhere in A6U01 forcing this field to 0.9999 if it would otherwise reach 1.0 or higher in the GROSS MARGIN sell method's percentage -- this vector demonstrates the field's raw storage capacity (up to 9.9999), not that clamped business rule, which operates on the logical value before storage, not on the encoding itself.

The field's declared default. Note this field has no confirmed 'N'/other explicit-not-error value in any source read this pass -- only 'Y' (error) and space (its own VALUE clause default) were found. Do not assume an 'N' value is ever set; this is CONFIRMED by absence, not a guess that it can't happen.

vectors.logical_value: LOW-VALUES (binary zero, not equal to 'Y' or space -- would NOT satisfy the OMGPR-PRICER-ERROR 88-level, since that only matches literal 'Y')
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (included as a decoder robustness case: a codec must not crash or silently mis-treat a low-values byte here as if it were a valid space/Y state)

vectors.notes: A real, confirmed error code from this codebase (docs/cobol-analysis/error-catalog.md and docs/rules/sell-selection-rules.md's R-SELL-003 item 10: gross-margin percentage-source defensive guard, 'INVALID WS-COST-CONTRACT SCENARIO FOR GRSSMGN').
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (two's-complement encoding of a real, documented error code)

vectors.notes: The highest confirmed OMGPR-Q-ERROR-NBR value actually assigned anywhere in A6U01.CBL (docs/cobol-analysis/error-catalog.md's mechanical scan of all 183 distinct codes, paragraph 7795-FIND-WHICH-JOIN-010). PIC S9(4) allows up to 9999, so this is far from the field's own storage ceiling -- included as the highest REAL value observed, distinct from V-UNITCOST-04/V-PCT-03's scale_max vectors which use the field's theoretical storage maximum instead.

A real, frequently-used literal from this codebase (WS-DB-STATUS-MSG, moved into OMGPR-ERROR-MESSAGE via WS-DB-OPERATION-MSG at essentially every fatal SQL-error site cataloged in docs/cobol-analysis/error-catalog.md section 1.2/1.3). Left-justified, space-padded to the full 76-byte field width. Only the 8 message-text bytes are given explicitly below; the remaining 68 bytes are the profile's own space byte (0x40 mainframe_ebcdic / 0x20 microfocus_ascii_native) repeated, not written out literally here to keep this file's size reasonable -- a decoder/encoder implementation must still produce all 76 bytes.
vectors.confidence: CONFIRMED (character encoding mechanism; message text choice is illustrative, drawn from a real confirmed literal)

what_was_scoped_out_of_this_pass: This is a representative set (8 fields, 23 vectors) spanning every OMGPR storage type (DISPLAY alphanumeric, DISPLAY date-as-text, COMP binary at two sizes, signed and unsigned COMP-3, and the dedicated error-output fields), not an exhaustive vector set for all 287 leaf fields in OMGPR.CPY. Extending this to full field coverage would follow the same method demonstrated here.

88-level condition fields beyond OMGPR-PRICER-ERROR (e.g. OMGPR-ACT-CNT-EXCL-EXISTS/-ABSENT) were not separately vectored -- they share the same underlying X(1) DISPLAY encoding mechanism already demonstrated by OMGPR-F-PRICER-ERROR.

The OCCURS-based repeating structures elsewhere in OMGPR were not vectored in this pass (OMGPR itself has none per program-inventory.md's field-inventory summary; OMGEXPL's OCCURS 700 array is covered separately by T004's own byte reconciliation, not duplicated here).
assumptions: COMP-3 packed-decimal layout is assumed profile-independent (identical bytes under both mainframe_ebcdic and microfocus_ascii_native) based on Micro Focus's own documented COMP-3/IBM-compatibility claim -- not independently verified against this specific deployment's actual Micro Focus configuration options.

OMGPR-D-PRICING's MM/DD/YYYY text layout (V-PRICING-DATE-01) is carried over from date-selection.md's own INFERRED reading of a similar substring-reassembly pattern elsewhere in A6U01 -- not confirmed by any comment local to OMGPR.CPY itself.
blockers: No live COBOL/CICS/DB2 execution environment to capture an authoritative COMMAREA byte dump and determine which encoding profile (or a third, unconsidered one) is actually in use -- standing blocker across this entire document set, and the specific blocker Codex's G1 review flagged as gating T017/T018 compatibility work.
OMGPR-D-PRICING's true external date format is not confirmed by any copybook comment.
